item.title: Armed robberies and sexual assaults cited in renewed US warning for island getaway
item.description: The renewed Bahamas travel advisory warns American travelers of violent crime, sexual assaults and armed robberies, with Nassau and Freeport cited as hot spots.
item.content:encoded:
Americans heading to the Bahamas are being reminded to exercise increased caution after the U.S. State Department renewed its travel advisory for the island nation.

The Bahamas remains under a Level 2: "Exercise Increased Caution" advisory, the State Department's second-lowest of four travel advisory levels.

The advisory, renewed this week, cited violent crime, burglaries, sexual assaults and armed robberies — reminding Americans that they can occur "anywhere in The Bahamas."

TRAVEL WARNING ESCALATES FOR POPULAR GETAWAY AS DANGERS AND SECURITY THREATS MOUNT

"Most crime occurs in Nassau and Freeport on New Providence and Grand Bahama islands," the State Department said.

"Stay alert in the 'Over the Hill' area in Nassau, south of Shirley Street, where gangs have killed residents."

The State Department also urged travelers to remain alert when staying at vacation rental properties, particularly those without private security.

VACATION HOT SPOT FACES NEW CDC TRAVEL WARNING AS OUTBREAK CASES CONTINUE CLIMBING

Officials also warned that boating in the Bahamas is not well regulated, noting that accidents have resulted in injuries and deaths.

"Due to safety risks, U.S. government employees are not allowed to use or rent jet skis and personal watercraft from independent operators on New Providence and Paradise Islands," the advisory read.

"Watercraft may not be safe, and some operators are not licensed or insured."

AMERICANS WARNED POPULAR TRAVEL ROUTES THIS SUMMER COULD CARRY CRIME AND KIDNAPPING RISKS

Officials are also urging visitors to stay alert on shore, citing reports of sexual assaults on and near downtown Nassau beaches.

"Never swim alone and beware of jet skis or other watercraft operating close to shore," the alert added.

"Stay alert for sharks. Shark attacks have led to serious injury and death."

The advisory also offers several personal safety recommendations for travelers, stating, "Do not answer your door at your hotel or residence unless you know who it is."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"Lock doors and windows and use other security features, especially on balcony doors," the warning added.

"Do not physically resist any robbery attempt."

Fox News Digital reached out to the State Department for further details. 

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

The renewed advisory comes as U.S. officials continue to warn travelers about crime at other tropical island destinations.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Earlier this summer, the State Department renewed its Level 2 "Exercise Increased Caution" travel advisory for Turks and Caicos, due to reports of assaults, petty crime and scams targeting tourists.

Recently, U.S. officials elevated Saint Lucia's travel advisory to Level 2, citing concerns about violent crime on the Caribbean island.

item.title: Cocky Curt Cignetti called out the SEC, but he should Google Indiana's laughable schedule first
item.description: Curt Cignetti took a vicious shot at the SEC during Big Ten Media Days, and fans quickly fired back by pointing out Indiana's soft schedule.
item.content:encoded:
The cocky Curt Cignetti train rolled on through Big Ten Media Days this week, and it doesn't seem like it's slowing down any time soon.

Nor should it, by the way. Indiana is the defending national champs. Cignetti has earned the right to be cocky. He's earned the right to pick fights with the SEC, and any other conference he chooses.

BUT, it will come to a halt at some point, and fans of a certain conference are already foaming at the mouth.

For those who missed it, Cignetti took a nasty little shot at the SEC on Thursday, calling out some unnamed teams — unofficially, of course — for making excuses.

INDIANA'S CURT CIGNETTI ROASTS THE SEC AS ESPN STARTS THEIR PROMOTIONAL CAMPAIGN ALREADY: 'WE DON'T WHINE'

"I mean we don’t run a hype machine up here in the Midwest," Cignetti said. "We believe everything’s earned, not given. And when we fall short, we say, ‘We fell short.’ We don’t cry a river, whine and complain. All right? And that’s why we’re the best."

Take a look:

Lordy. Just a vicious shot at the SEC. Again, Cignetti has earned the right to make it. The Hoosiers were dominant last year. But ...

Let's not get crazy. All these things tend to come out in the wash, and Indiana's schedule this upcoming season ain't exactly murderer's row.

SEC fans, of course, were QUICK to point that out yesterday:

I could go on and on. It's a war zone over on Elon's app formerly known as Twitter. Just a war zone. Which is great, because that means college football is almost back.

Less than 30 days, folks. Hang tight for just a bit longer!

Look, I'm an SEC guy. I'm biased. I'll happily admit that. OutKick's Ian Miller is not an SEC guy. He hates us. I get it.

I'm also a Florida Gators fan, and I'm man enough to admit the Hoosiers would probably crush us. They crushed just about everyone they faced last year, so it's safe to assume they'd do the same to us.

Now, they had a bunch of 30-year-old players on their team, but that's neither here nor there.

Relax, it's a joke! Sort of.

But, let's not act like Indiana is about to face the toughest schedule in the world. I mean, just look at that thing! It's hilariously bad.

That's a pathetic first six weeks. Come on. Let's be fair here. In that same span, LSU plays Clemson, Texas A&M and Ole Miss.

Texas plays Ohio State (!!!), Tennessee and Oklahoma.

Georgia plays Oklahoma and Alabama.

Oklahoma plays Michigan, Georgia and Texas.

Do we see the difference? Again, Cignetti can say what he wants and be as cocky as his heart desires. He's earned it. Indiana has earned it.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

But calling out the SEC for whining and complaining, while also knowing you have six straight bye weeks to open the season, is a ballsy move.

We'll see how this thing pans out.

Welcome back, college football.

item.title: KARR Bluetooth flaw exposes 2.2M cars to theft risk
item.description: A Bluetooth vulnerability in dealer-installed KARR and SWDS security devices puts 2.2 million vehicles at risk of being unlocked by nearby attackers.
item.content:encoded:
Could a small device hidden beneath your dashboard make your car easier to break into? Nancy from Newtown, Pennsylvania, asked me where she should look for the KARR or SWDS "code" in her 2025 Cadillac XT5 and 2024 Hyundai Tucson Limited Hybrid.

Here is the first thing you need to know. There is no code to find in your vehicle's settings. KARR and SWDS refer to aftermarket security hardware that a dealership may have installed before selling the car. SWDS stands for Southwest Dealer Services, the company associated with several KARR-branded vehicle protection products.

The device usually sits beneath the dashboard on the driver's side. You may also find a KARR or SWDS sticker on the driver-side window.

So, before you start searching through menus or calling the automaker, here is how to find out whether your vehicle has one of these devices and what to do next.

15 SECURITY ESSENTIALS TO KEEP YOUR VALUABLES SAFE FOR SUMMER TRAVEL

CyberGuy Live: Missed "Sick of Spam?" Get the replay and checklist

Our free CyberGuy Live class "Sick of Spam?" has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our spam-stopping checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you step by step through simple ways to reduce robocalls, spam texts, junk email and unwanted messages. You’ll also learn how to curb political texts, clean up your inbox and spot messages that could put your personal information at risk.

Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

Computer security researchers at the University of California San Diego uncovered a Bluetooth vulnerability affecting at least 2.2 million vehicles. The flaw involves dealer-installed KARR and SWDS security devices. A person standing within about five yards of a vulnerable vehicle could connect to the device through Bluetooth.

From there, an attacker could lock or unlock the doors. The same flaw could silence the alarm, sound the horn or flash the headlights. An attacker could also prevent a parked vehicle from starting. However, the researchers did not report that the flaw could start the engine or shut down a vehicle that was already running. That distinction is important. The Bluetooth flaw alone does not let someone drive away. However, it could quietly unlock the doors. A thief could then use separate tools to create or program a key.

KARR systems are aftermarket vehicle security products sold through participating dealerships. They may include an alarm, GPS tracking, remote vehicle controls or an ignition-disabling feature. Southwest Dealer Services uses several product names, including KARR Security, KARR Fusion, KARR BT, KARR S.W.A.T. and S.W.A.T. Dealer. The features vary by product and vehicle.

These devices do not come from Cadillac, Hyundai, Ford or another automaker's factory. A dealership or one of its vendors adds the hardware after the vehicle arrives. Dealers may use the system to protect inventory sitting on the lot. When someone buys the vehicle, the dealer may offer the system as an additional security package. The problem is that some dealers left the hardware connected even when buyers declined the service. As a result, a driver might have a vulnerable device without an active KARR account or any idea that the equipment is inside the car.

The KARR device communicates with a smartphone app through Bluetooth Low Energy. Researchers found that the affected devices relied on the same secret authentication key. Once they recovered that key, they could send commands that vulnerable KARR devices accepted.

Think of it as giving a huge group of devices the same unchangeable password. Once that password becomes known, each device becomes easier to approach. The researchers also found that the devices broadcast recognizable Bluetooth signals. Historical databases containing those signals could reveal where a particular device had appeared. That creates a privacy concern beyond car theft. Someone could potentially use the data to study where a vehicle regularly parks or travels.

UC San Diego researchers found the devices most often in vehicles sold through Honda, Toyota, Mazda, Ford and Jeep dealerships in Southern California since 2017. However, that list does not mean other brands are safe.

KARR works with more than 3,000 dealerships nationwide. Vehicles also move around the country through used-car sales, auctions and dealership trades. Therefore, the vehicle's make and model cannot confirm whether it has the equipment. The dealership that prepared the vehicle for sale matters more than the badge on the grille. A Cadillac, Hyundai or Chevrolet could have a KARR system if the selling dealer installed one. A Honda from another dealership might never have received it.

Start with the easy clues before you remove any trim or crawl too far beneath the dashboard.

Look at the lower corners and edges of the driver-side window.

The sticker may say:

A sticker strongly suggests that the dealership installed a related device. However, the absence of a sticker cannot completely clear your vehicle. A dealer or previous owner may have removed the label while leaving the hardware connected. UC San Diego says many affected vehicles have the sticker, rather than every affected vehicle.

Park the vehicle and shut off the engine. Move the driver's seat back and use a flashlight to look beneath the lower dashboard. Researchers say the device is usually installed underneath the dashboard on the driver's side.

You may see a small button or indicator light attached to the bottom edge of the dash. Wiring may run from the button behind the dashboard panels. The button shown by UC San Diego is small and easy to miss. It can look like a basic aftermarket alarm switch rather than a modern connected device. Do not pull on the wires or disconnect anything. The module may connect to the ignition system and other vehicle electronics.

Check the purchase agreement, dealer addendum, finance documents and service records.

Search for references to:

The charge may appear as part of a larger dealer protection package. You may also find the product listed with no separate price if the dealer installed it for inventory control.

TESLA HELPED SAVE A DRIVER; IS YOUR CAR READY?

Call the dealership that originally sold the vehicle. This step can help even when you bought the car used from another business. Your VIN appears near the bottom of the windshield on the driver's side. You can also find it on the registration, insurance card and driver-side door frame.

Ask the dealer: "Can you check this VIN and confirm whether your dealership or inventory vendor installed a KARR, SWDS, KARR BT, S.W.A.T. or other aftermarket security module?"

Then ask these follow-up questions: "Is the device still connected?" "Has it received the firmware update released on July 20, 2026?" "Can you provide the device model and firmware status in writing?"

A vague answer such as "Your factory alarm is fine" does not address the question. You are asking about dealer-installed aftermarket equipment.

KARR says people who never activated the security service can still use the official KARR Security app to check their VIN. Download the app only through the official Apple App Store, Google Play Store or KARR website. Do not use an app link from an unexpected text message, email or online advertisement.

After opening the app near the vehicle, tap the customer service link at the bottom of the screen. The app should guide you through the VIN check and available firmware update. KARR also lists customer support at 800-395-5277.

Nancy's 2025 Cadillac XT5 and 2024 Hyundai Tucson Limited Hybrid were not among the specific brands UC San Diego researchers said appeared most often. However, that does not rule them out. The device comes from the dealership rather than Cadillac or Hyundai.

Nancy should check each SUV separately. First, she should look for a KARR or SWDS sticker on the driver-side window. Next, she should use a flashlight to inspect the lower edge of the dashboard near the driver's knees.

She should also review the paperwork from each dealership. If the vehicles came from different dealers, one could have the equipment while the other does not. Finally, Nancy should call both selling dealers with the VINs. She should ask whether either dealership installed a KARR, SWDS or S.W.A.T. module before delivery. If the dealers cannot provide a definite answer, she can use the official KARR app or call KARR support.

Acrisure released a firmware patch on July 20, 2026, one day before UC San Diego publicly announced the vulnerability. The vehicle owner must deliver the update to the KARR device through the official KARR Security app. Updating your phone or vehicle infotainment system will not patch the separate module.

An activated system means you purchased or activated KARR service through the dealership.

Follow these steps:

KARR says no additional action is necessary after the app confirms that the latest firmware is installed.

You can still check and update a device that remained in the vehicle after you declined the service.

Follow these steps:

Call KARR support when the app cannot find the vehicle or complete the update.

WAYMO RECALLS ROBOTAXIS OVER CONSTRUCTION-ZONE RISK

You can ask to have the system deactivated or removed. However, I would not turn this into a weekend do-it-yourself project. Researchers warn that removal may require opening the dashboard, cutting wires and restoring connections involving the ignition system or vehicle computers. Disconnecting the wrong wire could stop the car from starting. It might also affect the factory alarm, remote start or another electrical feature. Southwest Dealer Services says an owner can request removal, transfer or deactivation by calling 800-395-5277 and confirming the account information.

Ask the original dealership or a qualified automotive electrical technician to handle the work. Before approving removal, ask the technician how the factory wiring will be restored. Afterward, request written confirmation that the module was removed and the vehicle's original security functions still work.

We reached out to KARR Security, and a representative from the company provided CyberGuy with the following statement:

"KARR Security maintains rigorous standards to help protect customers’ vehicles. Researchers at UC San Diego identified a vulnerability affecting BLE-based auto theft devices, including a small percentage of KARR devices with certain Bluetooth-related components. The vulnerability described in the research is highly complex and presents a low risk to customers under real-world conditions. Nevertheless, we responded promptly and developed a firmware update to address the issue. We launched this app/firmware update on July 20, 2026. Active customers may apply the update directly from their phone after securely logging in to the KARR Security app. Vehicle owners of non-active systems can still update via the app using their VIN (last 8 digits) as a validation step. Consumers can find detailed instructions and tutorials for assistance with this firmware on the Customer FAQ section of our website at www.KARRSecurity.com."

KARR Security added, "To our knowledge, we have not seen this vulnerability used in the real world to break into or steal a vehicle."

Turning off Bluetooth on your phone will not disable the Bluetooth radio inside the KARR module. Deleting the app will not remove the device. Removing the vehicle from your phone's normal Bluetooth menu will not patch it either.

The KARR module communicates separately from the Cadillac, Hyundai or other factory infotainment system. A Faraday pouch also will not fix this particular problem. Faraday pouches can help block relay attacks involving a key fob. They cannot update or disable hardware installed beneath the dashboard. You need to update the KARR device itself or have a professional remove it.

Car thieves use different methods, so protecting your vehicle requires more than one piece of technology.

When your vehicle has a KARR or SWDS device, install the firmware update as soon as possible. This directly addresses the Bluetooth flaw identified by the researchers. A steering wheel lock or tracker can add protection, but neither one repairs vulnerable software.

Signal jammers can sometimes block the command sent by a key fob. After pressing the lock button, listen for the normal confirmation sound. Look for the lights and pull a door handle before walking away. Also, close every window and take the keys with you. NHTSA recommends checking the doors whenever you leave a parked vehicle.

A steering wheel lock creates an obvious barrier inside the car. It will not stop every determined thief. However, it adds time and makes the vehicle harder to steer. NHTSA includes steering wheel locks among visible devices that can discourage vehicle theft. You can find more ideas in my CyberGuy guide on how to help prevent your car from getting stolen.

Store key fobs away from exterior doors, windows and attached garages. A tested signal-blocking pouch can help reduce the risk of a relay attack. In that type of theft, criminals extend the signal from a key inside the house to a vehicle outside. Test the pouch regularly. Put the key inside, close the pouch and stand next to the car. The doors should remain locked when you touch the handle. Remember that a key-fob pouch protects against a different attack. It will not patch a KARR module.

A hidden GPS tracker or Bluetooth tracker may help locate a stolen vehicle. However, do not confront anyone or attempt to recover the car yourself. Give tracking information to law enforcement. An Apple AirTag can provide a backup location signal, although Apple's anti-stalking alerts may eventually warn a thief that an unknown AirTag is traveling with the vehicle. Read my CyberGuy guide on using an AirTag in a vehicle and understanding its limits.

Use a locked garage when one is available. Otherwise, park in a visible area with lighting, foot traffic or a security camera. Avoid isolated corners where someone can work around the vehicle without attracting attention. NHTSA also recommends parking in well-lit areas whenever possible.

A thief may break into a car without planning to steal the entire vehicle. Take phones, laptops, wallets and bags with you. Do not leave a spare key or garage remote inside the car. NHTSA warns that thieves commonly target electronics and other items they can quickly resell.

Nancy's question highlights the biggest problem with this vulnerability. Many drivers have no idea that a KARR or SWDS device may be hiding in their vehicle. You will not find a KARR code inside your vehicle's settings. Look for a sticker on the driver-side window and a small aftermarket button below the dashboard. Then check your paperwork and ask the selling dealer to search your VIN. The flaw can unlock a vulnerable vehicle and interfere with its security features from nearby. It cannot start the engine by itself or shut down a moving car. Still, unlocking the doors may give a thief the access needed to try another method. Fortunately, KARR has released a firmware update. Install it through the official KARR Security app. When you no longer want the system, arrange professional removal rather than pulling wires yourself.

Should dealerships have to tell you about every connected device installed in your car, even when you decline to purchase the service? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

item.title: Michigan Senate candidate endorsed by AOC and Bernie Sanders insists he's not a socialist
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed insisted he is not a socialist despite his ties to DSA events, a Bernie Sanders endorsement and a new ad featuring AOC in the Michigan Senate race.
item.content:encoded:
Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed insisted during an interview on Tuesday that he was "simply not a socialist," when pressed on his close relationship with socialist figures such as Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., or Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y.

"Let me ask you about democratic socialism because you have a new ad with AOC in the ad," MS NOW's Jen Psaki asked. "You've been — you're very close to Bernie Sanders. You've had a number of these very popular officials come out and campaign for you. You've also said that you're not a democratic socialist. You describe yourself as a capitalist who understands capitalism." 

"But what is the difference? What are they getting wrong?" she continued. "I think this is confusing to a lot of people. What are they getting wrong about capitalism, or why don't you consider yourself a member of the democratic socialist movement? Given your proximity in your relationship to all of these officials."

"Because I'm simply not a socialist," El-Sayed said. "I believe in science. For me, you got to bring results. I've studied a lot of the solutions that I fight for, things like Medicare for All, things like rethinking the way that our financial system implies that corporate CEOs are more interested in a quarterly bottom line than they are in the long-term sustainability of their business."

SOCIALISM'S WAR ON SUCCESS HAS A NEW CHAMPION — AND HE’S RUNNING FOR SENATE IN MICHIGAN

El-Sayed is running in the Michigan Democratic Senate primary against U.S. Rep. Haley Stevens on August 4. The pair debated on Wednesday night and clashed on several issues.

He said that the U.S. operates in a monopoly or oligopoly when it comes to markets people are "forced" to participate in, adding, "I know that capitalism works, I just know that it does not work when you have monopolies or oligopolies."

"So, at the end of the day, it's just a philosophical difference," he continued. "I'm not an ideologue. I'm a lot more interested in empirical results. So, when it comes to Medicare for All, I think that's the best single way to provide folks healthcare in this country." 

"And by the way, public healthcare, the public part, would be the insurance," El-Sayed added. "The healthcare itself stays private. When it comes to investing in our schools or investing in good infrastructure, these are the shared resources that we need so that every single person can actually participate in the economy."

DEM CIVIL WAR HITS PRIMARY DEBATE STAGE IN FIERY BATTLEGROUND SHOWDOWN: 'WHAT ARE YOU HIDING?'

Psaki pressed him again and noted that socialists would say that they believe in science as well, saying, "If you're the nominee, Mike Rogers and the Republicans are going to try to label you as a democratic socialist. You're going to say you're not. But I'm saying, help us understand what's the difference between your version of capitalism and their version of democratic socialism."

El-Sayed then criticized Rogers, the presumptive Republican nominee for the Michigan Senate race.

"We're so concerned about what they're going to say about us that we forget that we also have mouths and can talk about that," El-Sayed said. "Let's talk about Mike Rogers. Mike Rogers is the worst kind of corporatist."

RAHM EMANUEL WARNS DSA AGENDA DOESN'T PLAY WELL OUTSIDE 'UPPER WEST SIDE OF MANHATTAN'

Alyssa Brouillet, the communications director for Rogers' campaign, told Fox News Digital in a statement, "We all know that if it walks like a duck, and quacks like a duck, it’s a duck. This election is about crazy versus common sense. Mike Rogers will hold the line against the Left’s socialist takeover and ensure common sense prevails this November." 

"It’s no surprise that the same guy who lied about being a physician is lying about everything else," the statement continued. "But while Abdul offers lip-service, Mike Rogers delivers results. Just today, Mike Rogers released a plan to fix our broken healthcare system by improving affordability, accessibility, and transparency of healthcare for working families."  

"This is only one of the many examples of Mike Rogers cleaning up the mess Democrats — like Abdul — created during their 32-year monopoly over Michigan’s two Senate seats," Brouillet added.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

El-Sayed has attended Democratic Socialist of America (DSA) events over the years.

Between 2017 and 2020, El-Sayed attended and spoke at six events held by the DSA, including a 2019 fundraiser which he headlined. El-Sayed has distanced himself from the DSA in interviews and has previously outright rejected being labeled as a "socialist."

"I'm not technically or practically DSA," El-Sayed told The Wall Street Journal earlier this month. In an interview with CNN, he similarly stated that "I am not somebody who is a socialist. I believe in capitalism, I just believe that capitalism has to be regulated."

At the 2019 event, which raised $10,000 for the organization, El-Sayed was described by DSA organizers as "a longtime friend of Detroit DSA." He was photographed smiling next to far-left Michigan Rep. Rashida Tlaib, a self-described socialist, behind a table with a poster on it depicting a hand labeled "DSA" choking a snake labeled "capitalism."

item.title: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Review: Tom Holland, Zendaya return for action-packed, emotional sequel
item.description: Fox News Digital reviews Sony Pictures and Marvel Studios' "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" starring Tom Holland, Zendaya, Sadie Sink, Jacob Batalon, Jon Bernthal and Mark Ruffalo.
item.content:encoded:
Your friendly neighbor Spider-Man… is going through some hard times. 

In "Spider-Man Brand New Day," Peter Parker (Tom Holland) is adapting to life in complete isolation in New York City. As you may or may not recall (based on the events of the film's 2021 predecessor "No Way Home"), Peter had everyone's memories erased after his identity had been exposed to the world, putting those he loved the most in danger. 

After having lost his Aunt May (Marisa Tomei), Peter vowed he wouldn't let what happened to her happen to the love of his life, MJ (Zendaya), nor his best friend, Ned (Jacob Batalon). So their memories of him are gone and his only connection to them is him stalking Ned's Instagram videos showing him and MJ living their best lives as students at MIT, something they talked about doing in high school.  

AS ‘THE ODYSSEY’ THRIVES AT THE BOX OFFICE, FRANCHISE FATIGURE HITS SUMMER WITH BOMBS LIKE ‘SUPERGIRL,’ ‘MOANA’ 

Meanwhile, a mysterious, telepathic villain is wreaking havoc in the Big Apple, jumping from body to body in the search for something dubbed "V-Max." This foe can take over anyone's mind, but meets its match with Spider-Man, of course.  

"Brand New Day" has a cast filled with familiar faces from the Marvel Cinematic Universe, like Bruce Banner aka The Incredible Hulk (Mark Ruffalo) and Frank Castle aka The Punisher (Jon Bernthal) as well as new ones like Detective Jean DeWolff (Liza Colón-Zayas of "The Bear" fame), who forms a partnership with Spider-Man — think a Batman/James Gordon dynamic — iconic Spider-Man foe Scorpion (Michael Mando) and Bill Metzger ("Severance" star Tramell Tillman), the chief of the U.S. Department of Damage Control created to repair the damage done from superhero fighting and contain whatever dangers that are left behind. 

I would be remiss if I didn't mention "Stranger Things" breakout Sadie Sink, whose involvement in "Brand New Day" has been kept under wraps — and for good reason, since her role is a bit of a game changer. Sink continues to be a rising star based on her string of compelling performances. 

'THE ODYSSEY' REVIEW: CHRISTOPHER NOLAN GOES EPIC WITH HIS MOST AMBITIOUS FILM TO DATE

The tone of "Brand New Day" is a bold departure from its three predecessors because of how Peter Parker grapples with loneliness, which is taking a toll on him physically — even affecting his superpowers. Tom Holland, fresh off the blockbuster hit "The Odyssey," will be web-slinging into another box office smash — but giving his strongest performance yet as Spider-Man, balancing the agony that his own isolation has brought him with the geeky charm audiences have grown to love over the years.

‘MOANA’ REVIEW: DWAYNE JOHNSON RETURNS FOR DISNEY'S LAZY LIVE-ACTION REMAKE THAT RESEMBLES AI SLOP

Zendaya — newly-married to Holland in real life, has plenty of on-screen chemistry with him for obvious reasons. And despite having her memory of Peter Parker erased in the last film, MJ has enough to work with (the same can't be said for Batalon's Ned, who's sadly sidelined here). Bernthal's The Punisher is a nice addition to the Spideyverse as the brute antihero has some comical exchanges with the lighthearted Spider-Man.

Destin Daniel Cretton, who previously directed Marvel's "Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings," takes over the director's chair from Jon Watts, who spearheaded the previous Holland "Spider-Man" films, though the screenwriting duo Chris McKenna and Erik Sommers, return for the fourth installment. 

There's a lot to balance in "Brand New Day" and Cretton handles it with care, particularly when it comes to the emotional elements to it — relying on a skill set he previously showcased in his highly underrated 2013 indie drama "Short Term 12." 

'THE INVITE' REVIEW: SETH ROGEN, OLIVIA WILDE HOST ONE HILARIOUS DINNER PARTY YOU WON'T REGRET ATTENDING

"Brand New Day" is more visually striking than its predecessors with well-choreographed action sequences. And Oscar-winning composer Michael Giacchino ("Up," "The Batman") delivers yet another fun score. 

With a nearly two-and-a-half hour running time, "Brand New Day" does drag a bit. And like many of the Marvel films, it doesn't present us with a truly great villain that superhero movies deserve (see Heath Ledger's Joker, Willem Dafoe's Green Goblin and Alfred Molina's Doc Ock in the Tobey Maguire "Spider-Man" trilogy, etc.) 

For the super Marvel fans out there, there is one post-credit scene at the end — offering a very mild teaser of what's to come for the beloved hero.

‘TOY STORY 5’ REVIEW: TOM HANKS, TIM ALLEN RETURN FOR TIMELY INSTALLMENT AS PIXAR GANG BATTLES RISE OF TECH

As the Marvel Cinematic Universe has broadly struggled in recent years, "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" gives it new life, thanks in large part to Holland at the helm. While it doesn't reinvent the wheel, this heartfelt superhero sequel will certainly satisfy fans and entertain audiences young and old. 

"Spider-Man: Brand New Day" is rated PG-13 for sequences of action/violence and some language. Running time: 2 hours, 25 minutes. In theaters now.

item.title: The Jacksonville Jaguars opened training camp with an amazing message about God on their social media
item.description: The Jacksonville Jaguars' faith-based post declaring "God is good" went viral with 1.9 million views, dwarfing their June Pride month post on social media.
item.content:encoded:
In a sports landscape that has included some biological males not only competing against, but sharing locker room space with biological females, leagues littering their fields or courts with stenciled woke signage, and teams celebrating Pride nights, wearing Pride warmup jerseys and even Pride-themed uniforms, we present the Jacksonville Jaguars this week.

The Jaguars, in case you are unfamiliar, are an NFL team in one of the league's smaller markets. They're also the defending AFC South champions.

And they're also the organization that put this on X this week:

"God is good ... All the time!

And then added a praying hands emoji.

That's quite a banger to start training camp.

SAN FRANCISCO GIANTS FANS PROTEST AND SHAME CHRISTIAN PITCHERS FOR BIBLE VERSES ON PRIDE NIGHT CAPS

Not surprisingly, people noticed.

The post was seen 1.9 million times as of Thursday evening after being posted at 10:18 a.m. on Wednesday.

The Jaguars boast around 857,000 followers on X, which is modest by NFL team standards. Their estimated average posts are viewed by anywhere from 20,000 to maybe 35,000 people.

BALTIMORE ORIOLES TAP DRAG QUEEN AS GUEST SPLASHER IN KID-FRIENDLY BIRD BATH ZONE FOR PRIDE NIGHT

But this simple message of faith went absolutely viral for the team.

It also became a curiosity because it's obviously atypical.

It's atypical because, first of all, it was posted by one of the several players who were given access to the team's account as a social media admin gimmick. And it worked.

"Rare Jags W, coming from a Texans fan," one fan replied.

A Colts fan agreed – the Jaguars, Colts and Texans are in the same division.

"Great message," another fan said.

"We're winning the Super Bowl," another offered.

Some fans added the "Jesus is Lord". Some fans asked if the post was referencing God or other gods.

But, as with everything on social media, there were those who did not forget the team's June 1 post on X. That one celebrated the start of Pride month.

Yes, the Jaguars were among the majority of NFL teams that proudly proclaimed their support for the LGBTQ movement on June 1.

That post, by the way, got 301,000 views — or about one-third as many as the one declaring God's goodness.

Anthony Fauci must face contempt of Congress, federal prosecution, and potentially arrest by the Senate sergeant-at-arms. And then, every state that had dealings with him should pursue charges independently.

Others were forced to homeschool their children as schools stayed closed for an absurd length of time. Poor kids, often minority, without adequate home resources faced tremendous learning loss, along with years of undetected neglect and mental, physical and sexual abuse that classroom teachers would have caught. Children suffered because schools, on Fauci's recommendation, ordered students to mask up, blocking the face-to-face interaction necessary for language and social development. Fauci told the world that the pandemic's origin was unknown; yet he suspected early on that the virus had emerged from a lab in Wuhan, China.
